scope: Final visible Draft; exact source, article, action-state, and deployed-JSON bytes; generation and publication timing; FleetRunner merged-PR count, restored-generation fencing, recovery and interruption qualification, roadmap gates, image runtime-user semantics; BookcaseDiscovery PR status, NS-K2 critical-path scope, clip metadata preservation; held action custody; and current review registry/discovery state. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: Seven core and BookcaseDiscovery PRs merged, not six
findings.location: The title, summary, and line 11 say six PRs merged across core and BookcaseDiscovery.
findings.explanation: The article names two merged core PRs (#591, #592) and five merged BookcaseDiscovery PRs (#92, #30, #93, #94, #96), all within the reporting window.
findings.correction: Say seven PRs merged across core and BookcaseDiscovery; if generated daily-logger #536 is included, distinguish it as an eighth listed editorial merge.

findings.title: Missing restored-generation configuration fails closed with HTTP 401
findings.location: Lines 39 and 67 and held action context say an unset FLEET_GENERATION silently disables the fence and produces no safety signal.
findings.explanation: Unset adapter configuration signs legacy request targets without a generation. The pinned restored service requires exactly one matching generation and rejects the request with HTTP 401, which the client surfaces as FleetHttpError.
findings.correction: Say omission is compatible only with a legacy-generation service; a restored service rejects it visibly. Describe the remaining operational configuration gap, and target BookcaseDiscovery #93 rather than nonexistent core #93.

findings.title: G6 is not downstream of G7 and its bounded work already ran
findings.location: Line 99 and retained context say G6, #593, and BookcaseDiscovery #95 cannot run until #594 merges and call restore capability suspended.
findings.explanation: Core #593 already records an 80-row interruption campaign and isolation proof; BookcaseDiscovery #95 has an exact-head source review and seven tests. #578 tracks G6 physical trials and G7 restores as separate gates. #594 already produced a held restored database while full G7 remains unqualified on transport and trial completeness.
findings.correction: Keep G6 and G7 separate. Preserve completed G6 source/campaign evidence and open physical trials; report #594's held restore plus the still-incomplete G7 transport and restore qualification; place G8 after the qualified prerequisites.

findings.title: Five BookcaseDiscovery PRs reported as open were merged
findings.location: Line 105 and retained lines 128-129 say #85 still needs exit review and group #85-#89 with open #59 as undispositioned open work.
findings.explanation: PR #85 records its conductor exit check and merged November 6; #86 and #87 also merged November 6; #88 and #89 merged November 8. Only #59 in the named set remained open.
findings.correction: Report #85-#89 as merged historical work with recorded outcomes and keep only #59 as open with its documented bounded daytime-test scope.

findings.title: NS-K2 explicitly maps thirty CLIs off the critical path
findings.location: Lines 53, 73, and 103 and the held decision action call the list approximately 25 and say its relationship to the next F-0 run was not mapped.
findings.explanation: PR #96 defines thirteen generalized stages as the critical path to TS-2, documents their stage order, and labels the untouched list off-path. Expanding KN-1 to KN-3 and C-5 to C-10, the article's list contains thirty CLIs.
findings.correction: Say thirteen stages were generalized for the declared path and thirty named CLIs remain explicitly off-path. Do not claim the mapping is missing or preserve the held decision action on that premise.

findings.title: The cited roadmap records document their open gates
findings.location: Line 99 and retained line 124 say what #578, #309, and #307 await is not documented.
findings.explanation: The latest #578 checkpoint names exact heads awaiting approval, unavailable management SSH, open physical trials, an unexecuted under-load backup, and unstarted G8. #309 says it is blocked by #311 and defines the host/reach decision. #307 says runtime implementation is not cleared while decisions remain active.
findings.correction: Summarize the documented gates and owners instead of treating a collector synopsis gap as absence from the primary issue records.

findings.title: The clip helper preserves metadata beyond the verified privacy checks
findings.location: The line 77 heading says no metadata leakage while line 79 says timed-metadata tracks are copied.
findings.explanation: The helper copies every non-audio track, asset metadata, per-track metadata, language codes, and metadata-track associations. PR #94 reports retained mebx tracks and separately verifies no location tag; that is not a blanket no-metadata-leakage result.
findings.correction: Say the pipeline removes audio and verifies no location tag while deliberately preserving other asset, track, and timed metadata; do not claim blanket no metadata leakage.

findings.title: The nonroot image default is overridable by Compose
findings.location: Lines 89-91 say a misconfigured Compose file cannot grant root and call the constraint unbypassable by operator configuration.
findings.explanation: The Dockerfile sets USER node, establishing the image default. Docker Compose's service-level user field overrides the image user declared by Dockerfile USER.
findings.correction: Say the image defaults to nonroot and the qualified profile ran nonroot. Treat it as a verified deployment/profile invariant, not an unbypassable property; runtime configuration can override it.
